reason: I want to transfer the frozen discovery safely, so placing its case at the cold transfer bench seems like a useful first step.
expectation: The case will be positioned for transfer; I am unsure what preparation the carrier will need.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the flight carrier at the bench also seems necessary, but I chose to bring the discovery there first.

effect: The discovery case is positioned at the cold transfer bench; the carrier still needs preparation.
reaction: Nothing notable; the placement was as expected.
reason: Preparing the flight carrier at the bench is the only available combination and should advance the transfer.
expectation: I expect the carrier to be prepared for receiving the frozen core, though I don't know exactly how.

effect: The carrier and transfer buffer are chilled to storage temperature and ready for the whole core.
reaction: The pre-chilling makes the transfer feel more deliberate, especially after the warming test showed how easily the layer can change.
reason: The case and conditioned carrier are ready at the bench, and combining them is the only available gameplay action.
expectation: I expect the body-bearing core and its surrounding ice to move into the conditioned carrier while remaining cold.

effect: The sealed core and neighboring ice are together in the flight carrier, ready for the refrigerated sample bay.
reaction: It is satisfying that the whole core made the transfer intact after the care taken to preserve its surroundings.
reason: Putting the packed core in the refrigerated bay is the only available gameplay action and should complete its transfer to flight cooling.
expectation: I expect the carrier to be secured in the lander's refrigerated bay, keeping the core cold for flight.

effect: The carrier is locked into the lander’s bay and connected to powered cooling, completing the transfer.
reaction: The thermal buffer bridging the transfer is a satisfying payoff to the earlier preparation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Moving the sealed liner with its neighboring ice into the chilled carrier was the most worthwhile action; it preserved the discovery’s surrounding layer as well as the body.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the case at the bench was the least engaging step; it was a straightforward preparation with little to discover on its own.

surprise.text: The carrier’s pre-chilled transfer buffer clarified how the core could stay cold while changing cooling connections.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each contributed to moving the core into flight cooling, although the placement itself was routine.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because I’m curious what Earth’s laboratory might learn from the intact core and its surrounding layer.
